text:
andrea: quick RFC follow-up — i'm proposing a "limited-trust bundle" API for on-prem/offline upgrades. goal: shrink agent TCB and let a verifier do most heavy crypto without needing full kms access on the appliance.

mike: curious — how's this different from our existing verifier + signed-delta bundles?

andrea: two differences: (1) explicit prepare/ attest/ apply phases so agent only stores artifacts until attestation succeeds, and (2) minimal runtime keys: agent only needs an ephemeral keypair for transport and an audit HMAC; all bundle signing keys live off-appliance or with a verifier process.

devon: sketch an API? short names pls so ops can script it.

andrea: proposed endpoints: `POST /v1/bundle/announce` (metadata only), `POST /v1/bundle/prepare` (stream content, agent writes to staging), `POST /v1/bundle/attest` (agent returns measurements), `POST /v1/bundle/apply` (final apply). attest is critical — verifier returns "ok/fail" and signed apply-token. agent only accepts apply if token present.

priya: what does the attestation payload look like? we need it small for constrained devices.

andrea: minimal fields: bundle_id, staged_hashes (sha256 per artifact), boot-id, firmware-version, free-space, optional hw-tpm-pcr. Example:```json
{
  "bundle_id": "b-2026-03-20-01",
  "staged": [{"path":"/var/stage/rootfs.img","sha256":"..."}],
  "boot_id": "abc123",
  "tpm_pcr": null
}
```

mike: how do we keep rollbacks safe? if apply partially succeeds and we lose power, ops panic.

andrea: make apply idempotent + two-phase swap: write new artifacts to new image slot, update boot metadata atomically, provide a short grace window where rollback is automatic unless a heartbeat to control-plane is seen. if apply fails, agent reverts to previous slot.

devon: delta vs full bundle tradeoff? our customers have tiny flash sometimes.

andrea: support multi-mode: (A) index-first deltas when device has enough working-set, (B) single-file atomic images for tiny devices. Bundles carry a lightweight manifest that tells agent which mode to use.

sec-bot: security note: verifying signer chain off-appliance reduces key compromise risk but increases dependency on the verifier's availability. need offline verification mode (preloaded root certs) for fully air-gapped sites.

priya: UX: ops team wants a single CLI that handles announce->prepare->apply with auto-retry. also expose `bundle status <id>` to inspect staged artifacts and last attest result.

mike: operationally we should require an expiry timestamp on apply-tokens so stolen tokens can't be reused indefinitely. short TTL (5m?) + nonce.

andrea: agreed. apply-token = signed{bundle_id, agent_id, nonce, expiry, mode}. verifier signs with offline key. agent validates signature and expiry before applying.

devon: metrics & observability: emit events for each phase (announce/prepare/attest/apply/rollback) and attach small diagnostics blob on failure. ops can ship via existing collector when network available.

priya: would this change the bundle transport format? want to avoid introducing new heavy protocols.

andrea: transport stays HTTP(s) and supports chunked streaming for large artifacts. manifest + metadata are compact json. for extreme air-gapped installs we also accept tarball blobs on USB with the same manifest layout.

mike: final question: backward compatibility with current agent? we need a migration plan.

andrea: plan: (1) agent vX adds compatibility shim — accept old-style bundles and map into prepare/attest/apply flow; (2) rollout verifier that emits apply-tokens; (3) after 2 release cycles we deprecate old endpoints.

sec-bot: outstanding threat modelling items: (A) replay of announce->prepare sequence, (B) stale manifests with valid signatures, (C) compromised verifier signing key. recommend: nonces + manifest versioning + key-rotation support + cross-signed timestamps.

andrea: next steps: i'll update the RFC with endpoint payloads, token format, and the two-slot apply algorithm. if no blockers i'll open a cleanup ticket for agent shims and an integration test matrix for tiny/medium/large devices. :thumbsup:

mike: +1 from eng-platform. can you also add a short example of tpm-based attestation path in the RFC?

andrea: yes — will add a TPM appendix and a 1-paragraph ops runbook for USB-driven installs.

opsbot: deploy-bundle job queued for testing in staging cluster (job: db-ctx-42).
